voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: From December nineteen eighty-one, people in the Hessdalen valley, in central Norway, reported lights in the sky. Up to twenty times a week.
White, yellow, or red. Some hovered in mid-air for more than an hour. Others moved off at enormous speed.
In nineteen eighty-three, researchers came to watch the valley, with cameras, and radar.
Since nineteen ninety-eight, an automatic station has watched the sky there, day and night.
Proposed explanations include burning dust, and rock under strain. More than forty years on, there is no agreed explanation.
